key_insight: A lightweight transfer-learning upgrade to BiSeNetV2 makes weld-seam segmentation far more robust to reflections without increasing model complexity.
engineering_relevance: This improves real-time robotic welding perception in construction, where thin seams and specular metal surfaces often cause segmentation failures.
method: Transfer-learned BiSeNetV2 backbone for seam segmentation
Hybrid Cross-Entropy + Lovász loss to stabilize learning
Focus on reflection-robust optimization rather than adding layers
evidence_signal: The method reached 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU, with +22.36 percentage points Joint IoU over the OHEM baseline while keeping FLOPs, parameter count, and inference speed unchanged.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown on the reported welding dataset and may need revalidation on different cameras, metals, and site lighting conditions before deployment.
paper_title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
